mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen in each of the last three weeks (-23.3 to -13.4), showing that commuting and errand trips are being re-added to daily routines. This mobility momentum decays slowly, so RETAIL_REC keeps climbing over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is below its last 28-day mean while TRANSIT continued to print higher weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen from 4.4 to 0.7, meaning households are spending fewer hours at home than at any point in the window. Each point of residential decline releases time and spending into out-of-home discretionary activity, lifting RETAIL_REC.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL prints below +1.5 for a week and RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is at or below its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES (-22.7 to -6.6) and TRANSIT (-23.3 to -13.4) are recovering jointly, which is the signature of offices and shops reopening together rather than a single-sector bounce. Joint recovery multiplies weekday retail footfall beyond either series alone.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean above -10 and TRANSIT weekly mean above -15 in the same week
failure_condition: In weeks where WORKPLACES is above -10 and TRANSIT above -15 simultaneously, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is not higher than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS swung from 12.7 to 50.3 in one week, a weather-driven outdoor-leisure shock rather than a retail signal. Favorable-weather outdoor trips are complements to errand trips, so the park surge pulls RETAIL_REC up on a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean rises more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from 12.7 to 50.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS rises more than 20 points week-on-week, the following week's RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the triggering week's mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM printed at or above +10 in t-1w before easing to 9.9, the classic stockpiling-and-caution signature. Households that re-stock are protecting against renewed disruption, so discretionary RETAIL_REC falls over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM weekly mean at or above +10
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 5.6 to 12.4 then eased to 9.9
failure_condition: After a GROCERY_PHARM print at or above +10, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean exceeds its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES crossing above -10 is the observable marker that work-from-home advisories have been relaxed and capacity limits are being lifted in sequence. Each policy relaxation step adds retail capacity, so RETAIL_REC rises over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES weekly mean exceeds -10 for the first time in the window
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -22.7 to -6.6 across four weeks
regime_hint: late-stage reopening with capacity limits still binding
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES crosses above -10, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is lower than or equal to its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has risen every week (-17.4, -12.1, -10.7, -8.9) with no reversal. Autocorrelated mobility recovery of this shape persists week-to-week, so the next week's RETAIL_REC mean is above the current mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose monotonically across all four weekly means
failure_condition: The very next weekly RETAIL_REC mean is below -8.9, breaking the monotone four-week ascent.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS above +40 while RESIDENTIAL drops below +1.5 means discretionary out-of-home time is being allocated to open-air recreation instead of indoor retail. Under warm-weather reopening, this substitution diverts spend away from RETAIL_REC for a month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above +40 while RESIDENTIAL weekly mean is below +1.5
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS printed 50.3 in t-0w while RESIDENTIAL fell to 0.7
failure_condition: In weeks where PARKS is above +40 and RESIDENTIAL below +1.5, RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean is higher than its last 28-day mean.
